title: why a note cannot be found by the symbol it is about
summary: A note's searchability is decided by the SPEC SHAPE the capture prompt publishes, not by the matcher or by how well the note is written — and the default shape omits the one field the anchor channel is built for. kbSearch weights anchors (paths AND declared symbols) at x2 precisely so a code-shaped query like `cmdSearch` or `mintToken` can land, but WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES publishes file-single as {type, path, summary, aliases} with no symbols field, and file-single is the default for ~97% of notes. Measured 2026-08-01: 2 of 44 notes in this notebook declare any anchor symbol. So agent-issued kb search queries — mined from 86 local transcripts: 38 queries, median 4 words, half containing a code-shaped token — have nothing to match but prose, and the right note lands at rank 2 behind a neighbour that shares generic words (`cmdSearch context` ranked the coverage flow above src/kb/cli.ts; `alias cap fold` ranked the test note above src/kb/fold.ts). The storage layer was never the constraint: write.ts accepts anchors[{path,symbols}] on a file spec and unions them in. Nothing about this is visible in hook-mode measurements, because hook mode's own gates are what everyone has been tuning.

steps.role: publishes the file-single shape agents copy — omits symbols, so none are ever supplied
accepts and unions anchors[{path,symbols}] on file specs — the capability exists, unused
weights the anchor channel x2 for exactly these terms, and finds it empty

invariants: The anchor channel can only hold what the spec shape asks for — a matcher change cannot recover a field agents were never told to write.
file-single is the default and ~97% of volume, so anything missing from ITS shape is missing from the corpus.

Tool-mode (kb search) quality is invisible in the inject log: cli.ts logs inject-log only when flags.hook, so tool hits have never been recorded — one tool-source query exists in the entire history, a miss.

The same defect hit aliases: the capture prompt inlines its OWN copy of the shapes and that copy had lost "aliases" from the flow shape, so flows written from it were reachable only by their exact title. Neither was a schema limit — write.ts accepted anchors[{path,symbols}] on file specs the whole time. Both shapes now carry both fields, kb write reports missing findability fields with a ready-to-paste re-put, and a parity test pins the two copies together. THE GENERAL LESSON: a field agents are never asked for is a field the corpus will not have, and no matcher change can recover it; when a shape has two copies, the drift is silent and shows up as a retrieval gap months later.

title: why a note cannot be found by the symbol it is about
summary: CORRECTED 2026-08-01 (second pass — the first version of this note got the mechanism wrong; trust this paragraph over anything above it). A note's stored anchor symbols matter in HOOK mode only. Verified by running kbSearch both ways on `cmdSearch context` and reading carriers: lane 2 (resolveTermToSymbolFiles over the keeper's kb-notes.json sidecar, which holds a per-anchored-file symbol inventory — 35 of 47 files here, and it does contain cmdSearch for src/kb/cli.ts) is ENABLED in tool mode and DISABLED in hook mode at search.ts:488, because enabling it there produced false implants. So `kb search` can match a symbol a note never stored, while hook recall cannot. The shape gap was still real — file-single published no symbols field, so 2 of 44 notes stored any, and hook mode had nothing — but the earlier claim that the anchor channel is empty CORPUS-WIDE was wrong for tool mode. Beware attributing rank changes to this: after storing symbols on src/kb/cli.ts its note went from rank 2 to rank 1 in BOTH modes, but the summary was rewritten in the same write, so the cause is not isolated. Aliases have no such fallback in either mode: nothing derives them, so a note without them is reachable only by its exact title, and the capture prompt's inlined copy of the flow shape had silently lost the field.
invariants: Lane 2 (sidecar symbol inventory) is tool-mode ONLY — search.ts:488. Stored anchor symbols are the only symbol evidence hook mode has.
Aliases have no derived fallback anywhere; a note without them is reachable only by its exact title.
The anchor channel can only hold what the spec shape asks for — a matcher change cannot recover a field agents were never told to write.
Two copies of a shape drift silently; tests/kb-shape-parity.test.ts is what makes it loud.
Findability checks REPORT, never reject: the capture prompt chains writes with && so a non-zero exit silences every note behind the failing one.
